name: Foursquare Listings

sources.title: Foursquare for Business — 'Search for your business on Foursquare' / 'Claim your listing' landing page
Claim flow — JS/Auth0-driven, returned no readable content to a plain fetch

conditions: Claiming and managing a listing is free, but the flow is gated behind an Auth0 account login
Only meaningful for a real physical/local venue — the claim flow starts by searching for an existing venue by name/location
requirements: The business must exist (or be addable) as a Foursquare venue with a real-world location — this is a local-business directory, not a SaaS/product directory
Claim requires signing into a Foursquare account (Auth0-based auth on business.foursquare.com)
Verification/ownership checks apply to manage a venue listing
preparation: Business name, address, phone, category, and hours
Proof of association with the venue if ownership is challenged
workflow: Open https://business.foursquare.com/ and use 'Search for your business on Foursquare' to find the venue
If the venue exists, click through to claim it and sign in
If the venue does not exist, add it via the consumer-side add-venue flow (foursquare.com app/site) first
Complete the claim and manage listing details from the business dashboard
watchFor: business.foursquare.com is a JS/Auth0 SPA — plain fetches return empty or 'auth0-spa-js must run on a secure origin' errors; requires a real browser session
Poor fit for online-only SaaS: the catalog is venues (bars, restaurants, boutiques), so claiming a software product is not a legitimate route
Paid upsells (Foursquare ads/promoted placement) exist but are not required to claim
countsAsLive: The venue's public Foursquare page shows claimed/verified status and the managed details are visible to consumers
unknowns: Exact verification method and review turnaround for claims
Whether new venues can be added directly from business.foursquare.com or only via the consumer app
Whether listing edits propagate to Foursquare City Guide immediately
